newsitem.title: USA: TCF Financial, Winthrop close deal.
newsitem.headline: TCF Financial, Winthrop close deal.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Tuesday its merger with Winthrop Resources Corp was completed after shareholders of both companies approved the merger.

As a result of the merger, each common share of Winthrop is being exchanged for 0.7766 of one common share of TCF, for a total of about 6.9 million TCF common shares. The total merger price is about $340 million or $38.05 per Winthrop common share, based on TCF's closing stock price of $49 per share on June 23.

On February 14, TCF and Winthrop signed a letter of intent to merge, which was followed on February 28 with the signing of a definitive merger agreement. TCF received regulatory approval from the Federal Reserve Board on June 2.
Winthrop is now a wholly owned subsidiary of TCF. John Morgan will continue as president of Winthrop and has joined TCF's board of directors.
The merger transaction is being accounted for as a pooling of interests.

Winthrop is a Minneapolis-based financial services company that leases computers, telecommunications equipment, point-of-sale systems and other business equipment to companies nationwide. At March 31, Winthrop had leased assets totaling $348 million.
TCF is a bank holding company based in Minneapolis with $7 billion in assets. TCF's banks operate in Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan and Ohio.
